First, we express $y$ as the composite function

$$
y=\sqrt{u},\,u=\operatorname{csc}⁡v,\,v=5x+2.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}},\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}v}=-\operatorname{csc}⁡v\operatorname{cot}⁡v,\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=5.
$$

Applying the chain rule twice, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}v}\cdot \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}\cdot (-\operatorname{csc}⁡v\operatorname{cot}⁡v)\cdot 5 \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{\operatorname{csc}⁡(5x+2)}}\cdot (-\operatorname{csc}⁡(5x+2)\operatorname{cot}⁡(5x+2))\cdot 5 \\  & =-\frac{5}{2}\operatorname{cot}⁡(5x+2)\sqrt{\operatorname{csc}⁡(5x+2)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now we compute ${y}^{′}(0):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(0) & =-\frac{5}{2}\operatorname{cot}⁡(5(0)+2)\sqrt{\operatorname{csc}⁡(5(0)+2)} \\  & =-\frac{5}{2}\operatorname{cot}⁡(2)\sqrt{\operatorname{csc}⁡(2)}.\end{aligned}
$$
